thread:
Jamie: FYI ran a synthetic 1k-burst on the nyc pool. p99 shows a clear staircase during scale-up; each allocation step bumps tail then it relaxes.
Jamie: quick summary: p95 ~78ms; p99 jumps at worker steps: ~220ms -> 380ms -> 610ms (corresponds to 3,6,12 workers). observed kv miss spike right after each step: 6% -> 28%.
Akash: do we have kernel-selector logs for the window? wondering if kernel flips align with the p99 cliffs.
Jamie: pasted trimmed runtime log lines:
```
[12:04:02] kernel_selector: choose=fast_attn_v2 batch=4 load=0.32
[12:04:03] kernel_selector: switch -> compat_attn batch=8 reason=queue_depth=9
[12:04:04] kv_cache: miss_rate 0.06 -> 0.28 (policy=LRU)
```
Jamie: kernel switch lines line up with the first p99 jump. note switch occurred right after autoscaler step when microbatcher increased aggregation.
Akash: hypothesis: autoscaler step -> transient queue spike -> batcher aggregates more -> selector picks larger-batch kernel -> short-lived kernel path has worse tail for these short sequences.
Lina: infra detail: new worker joins trigger kv shard sync; until sync completes the miss rate rises and causes extra backend latency.
Sara: so two overlapping causes: kernel-switch cost + kv cold-sync. need a mitigation order.
Akash: my proposal: (1) short kernel-switch hysteresis after scale events (5-15s), (2) cap aggressive microbatch growth during the "runway" window, (3) prefer small-batch kernels when kv_miss_rate > threshold.
Akash: config prototype:
```
kernel_switch_hysteresis_secs = 12
batcher:
  max_microbatch_during_scale = 4
kv_miss_gate_pct = 10
```
Jamie: kv_miss gate seems simplest and effective. also add per-worker kv_sync_time histograms to runs.
Lina: infra alternative: keep a tiny warm "stager" pool (2-3 nodes) that absorb initial traffic while main pool ramps. reduces mass kernel flips and kv fanout.
Sara: tradeoff is cost. could we instead prime KV on joining workers? do async prefetch on join to reduce service miss window.
Akash: priming seems doable: on join, fire off background prefetch of top-N shards. adds join step but avoids p99 shock.
Jamie: experiment plan A/B:
A) implement kernel-switch hysteresis + kv_miss gate + "staircase-smoothing" batching
B) enable stager pool + prefetch-on-join
Run 50 bursts each, compare p95/p99, batch_size_hist, kernel_switch_count, kv_miss_rate, kv_sync_wall_time, worker_join_time.
Sara: add trace tag on requests that hit a kernel-switch path so we can correlate event -> request latency. sample tags: runtime.event=kernel_switch, runtime.kv_miss=1
Akash: pseudocode for stair-smoothing:
```
if time_since_last_scale < 10s:
  batcher.aggregation_factor = max(1, default_agg/2)
```
Jamie: action items:
- Akash: implement hysteresis, kv_miss gate, stair-smoothing flag (branch perf/stair-safety)
- Lina: provision stager profile + staging cluster for B
- Sara: instrument traces + build experiment dashboard
- Jamie: schedule A/B runs and collect per-kernel p99 tables
Akash: will add runtime flag `scale_safety_mode` so we can toggle without redeploy.
Lina: I'll also capture kv_sync_time histogram per worker and log join timeline.
Sara: include rollback plan: if hysteresis harms throughput, reduce hysteresis to 3s or disable flag.
deploy-bot: scheduled: deploy perf/stair-safety branch to staging at 2026-03-19T08:45Z (canary 5%) :rocket:
Jamie: final note: include a post-run matrix of kernel-version vs p99 by batch-size; helps isolate which kernel path penalizes short seqs.
Akash: good call. I'll add that to the run reporter.
Jamie: thanks all :thumbsup:
